name: Olissippo Lapa Palace
positioning: A 19th-century former private residence in Lisbon, overlooking the Tagus River and surrounded by subtropical gardens
best_for: Travelers who want a historic palace with gardens and a pool in Lisbon
Families who want babysitting and a kids' pool

facts.text: The palace was built in the 19th century as a private residence.
The hotel overlooks the Tagus River.
The palace sits atop one of Lisbon's seven hills.
The hotel's address is Rua do Pau de Bandeira, 4, in Lisbon.
Rooms in the former palace are individually decorated, and some have garden or city and river views.
Bathrooms are marble and stocked with L'Occitane products.
Portraits of the manor's former occupants hang throughout the hotel.
Le Pavillon serves canapes and drinks poolside.
Le Pavillon hosts barbecues every Thursday through the summer.

highlights.text: The hotel is surrounded by subtropical gardens.
The rooms have different decorative styles: art deco, colonial, Algarve and neoclassical.
The garden has fountains, fish ponds and an outdoor pool.
The Rio Tejo Bar offers afternoon tea from May through September.
The hotel offers babysitting services and has a kids' pool.

considerations.text: Navigating the grounds can be disorienting, so guests can ask for a map at check-in.
Afternoon tea at the Rio Tejo Bar is seasonal, from May through September.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Olissippo Lapa Palace Hotel
